# ecoplus_server (Resource)

A Hetzner Cloud server leased from the ecoplus pool. Destroying it wipes the disk and returns the server to the pool until just before its next billed hour.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ecoplus_server" "sandbox" {
  name        = "sandbox-1"
  server_type = "cx22"
  location    = "nbg1"
  image       = "ubuntu-24.04"
  ssh_keys    = ["deploy"]

  labels = {
    team = "platform"
  }
}

resource "hcloud_firewall_attachment" "sandbox" {
  firewall_id = hcloud_firewall.default.id
  server_ids  = [tonumber(ecoplus_server.sandbox.id)]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `image` (String) Image name or snapshot ID. Changing it rebuilds the server in place.
- `location` (String) Hetzner location, for example `nbg1`. Changing it replaces the server.
- `name` (String) Server name, an RFC 1123 hostname label unique within the Hetzner project. Changing it renames the server in place.
- `server_type` (String) Hetzner server type, for example `cx22`. Changing it replaces the server.

### Optional

- `labels` (Map of String) Labels applied to the server while you hold it. Keys must not start with `ecoplus/`. Cleared when the server is released.
- `ssh_keys` (Set of String) Names of Hetzner SSH keys to install. Changing the set replaces the server.
- `user_data` (String) Cloud-init user data, at most 32 KiB. An empty string is treated as unset. Changing it replaces the server.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Hetzner server ID.
- `ipv4_address` (String) Public IPv4 address.
- `ipv6_address` (String) Public IPv6 address.
- `lease` (String) Lease ID fencing this resource to the server.
- `reused` (Boolean) Whether the server came from the pool instead of being freshly created.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ecoplus_server.sandbox 12345678/0123456789abcdef
```
